classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that slant sides are irrelevant and that area depends only on the base and the distance between the parallel lines. Part c then reverses the formula using an area from a previous part.

content.prompt: Parallelograms $P$, $Q$ and $R$ are drawn between two parallel lines that are $12\text{ cm}$ apart.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Calculate the area of each parallelogram.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}A&=bh\\A&=8\times12\\A&=96\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$$
The 13 cm and 15 cm sides are not the height. All three have base 8 cm and height 12 cm.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Parallelogram $S$ is drawn between the same two parallel lines. It has a base of $8\text{ cm}$ and a slant side of $40\text{ cm}$. Find its area.

children.label: c
children.prompt: A parallelogram has a base of $12\text{ cm}$ and a slant side of $9\text{ cm}$. Its area is equal to the area of parallelogram $Q$. Find its perpendicular height.
